summary: Two small corrections: plants cross oceans more readily than animals, not less (which is why their lines are blurrier), and I cut the line saying cockatoos live on Lombok but not Bali, which is no longer true. Everything else checked out, including every quotation.

changes.before: Plants, which cross oceans less readily than animals, may draw blurrier lines still.
changes.after: Plants, which cross oceans more readily than animals, may draw blurrier lines still.
changes.why: The source says plants tend to disperse across oceans better than animals, and that is the reason their divisions may be less clear. The draft had it backwards.

changes.before: The line is still visible today. Cockatoos live on Lombok but not on Bali. Sulawesi
changes.after: The line is still visible today. Sulawesi
changes.why: Not true today: the yellow-crested cockatoo is probably extinct on Lombok, while a remnant population survives on Nusa Penida in Bali province. Wallace himself noted a few cockatoos in west Bali. A peripheral detail, cut cleanly.

notes: Wallace's reply to Darwin about Earl survives only as quoted in later scholarship (Fichman 1977, via the ANU Press chapter); the letter itself has not been found. The wording matches that source.
The two doi.org links were confirmed against independent records (HKU Scholars Hub and the University of Amsterdam repository) rather than opened directly.
